findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that backfill_from_managed_refs skips any key that already has a record (or otherwise guards against overwriting an existing push/snapshot record), since the landed record() overwrites unconditionally — AC5's no-downgrade half depends on a guard the scope does not describe.
evidence: S1 peer_confirmations.py record(): self._records[key] = {... 'source': source_kind ...}; self._dirty = True — unconditional overwrite, no provenance comparison
AC5: 'a backfill never overwrites an existing "push" or "snapshot" record (provenance upgrades, never downgrades)'
S4 Scope: 'write a record keyed (ticket_local_id, target, kind) with source="backfill"' — no guard described
findings.finding: AC5's no-downgrade guarantee ('a backfill never overwrites an existing push or snapshot record') is not achievable by the mechanism the plan names: S1's landed PeerConfirmationStore.record() unconditionally overwrites the record at a key, and the S4 scope describes backfill only as unconditionally 'writing a record' with source='backfill'. No read-before-write / skip-if-present guard is specified, so a backfill firing on a key that already carries a push/snapshot record would clobber (downgrade) it.
scenarios: A managed ref already has a push record (S1) from a prior run, then a fresh checkout with an absent store triggers backfill on the same key — the push record is downgraded to backfill, losing the vendor link_id.
findings.suggested_fix: In backfill_from_managed_refs, before writing, check store.get(source, target, kind) is None (or store.is_confirmed(...)) and skip when a record already exists; only write for keys with no prior record.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Align the backfill record() call with S1's landed API: pass source_kind=SOURCE_BACKFILL, and introduce a DIRECTION_BACKFILL constant (or reuse an existing direction) rather than an ad-hoc direction="backfill" string.
evidence: S1 record() signature: record(..., *, link_id, direction=DIRECTION_OUTBOUND, pass_id, source_kind=SOURCE_PUSH)
S1 defines SOURCE_BACKFILL='backfill' but no DIRECTION_BACKFILL; DIRECTION_* is outbound|snapshot only
S4 Scope: 'source="backfill", direction="backfill"'
findings.finding: The record() call parameters in S4's scope do not match S1's landed API vocabulary. S1's record() takes keyword source_kind (not source), and its documented direction values are only outbound|snapshot (constants DIRECTION_OUTBOUND/DIRECTION_SNAPSHOT). S4 specifies source="backfill" and direction="backfill" — the latter is a novel direction value with no constant.
scenarios: Implementer passes source= as a positional/keyword that does not exist, or invents an undocumented direction value inconsistent with the store's two-value direction vocabulary.
findings.suggested_fix: Use store.record(ticket_local_id, target, kind, link_id=None, direction=DIRECTION_BACKFILL, pass_id=pass_id, source_kind=SOURCE_BACKFILL) and add DIRECTION_BACKFILL to peer_confirmations.py.

findings.finding: The backfill mechanism as specified will DOWNGRADE existing provenance, contradicting its own AC5. backfill_from_managed_refs is told to 'write a record ... with source="backfill"' with no guard, but PeerConfirmationStore.record() overwrites unconditionally. On a fresh-upgrade pass, handle_update writes source="push" records during _apply_mutations (reconcile.py:203) BEFORE backfill runs in _persist_and_log (reconcile.py:204). Backfill would overwrite those push records with source="backfill".
findings.suggested_fix: State that backfill consults store.get(...) (or is_confirmed) per key and writes only when absent — never overwriting an existing record — which satisfies AC5's no-downgrade half directly and leaves the snapshot upgrade (S2, running after backfill) to overwrite backfill records.
